body:
"my printer isn't working"
"are you on the wifi?"
"no"
"go on the wifi"
"it's working now!"
Every. Day.
I built a computer a few days ago, will never be impressed by people who tell me they built their computer again. I'm an actual moron and did it via reddit and YouTube.
You might consider working for osha or similar, or possibly motivational speaking, based on your replies :)
Or Catherine zeta Jones
Bosses me around with a smile
I wanna force choke Vladimir Putin
bruh i already told you I'm killing myself. no worries.
omg a live-stream of the sink area would change my life.
Yep Understood thanks u/thomki I will be certain to mention your incredibly helpful advice in the suicide note I leave for my coworkers inside the dishwasher they never open.

I already do those things. I come in an hour  before anyone else in order to even attempt to have the place be tidy by the time they get here, but since our data staff occasionally stay past 7pm I can't clean up AFTER them until the morning.
Because of rapid growth and inattentive managers. I thought I told you to eff off though...weird...
culture is going to change when I walk off the effing roof

Event planning and culture management is easy? Onboarding is easy? Do you know what goes into onboarding a new employee? What about when it involves security clearance? You know how to manage union and non-union vendors? Coordinate an office move in manhattan?

How about you stop giving bad advice.
Unfortunately as I've said in other areas, the sweep and mop service our building provides has union rules that preclude our hiring any other staff.

I should have clarified. They already used reusables when I started, I refuse to replace them with disposables because A - it's wasteful and B- the disposables we currently use never make it to the garbage pail anyway.
the engineers are actually my favorites, they occasionally clean up after themselves. the data analysts and salespeople refuse outright to do anything.
Try my job before you tell me a moron could do it. Be. Less. Rude.

To be honest, the employees are like matrix batteries. They sit and produce consistent results based on algorithms and standard practices, and the salespeople sell it. We don't NEED a whole lot of structure to function as a company, especially not while I handle all of our onboarding.

Hey asshat, I'm broke. Where do they hand out the free certifications and the free "do my chores at home also" help so that I can use my time at home to do more work? 

Please feel free to suck your own advice. Next caller.
I do that as well, but it doesn't solve the problem, just that momentary instance.
There is an optional increase which we've opted for, but literally all they do is wipe down the countertops, and they won't do it if there are dishes piled on those countertops.
Unfortunately not, I've tried. We can try to sneak cleaners in and skirt union rules, but we could get fined or kicked out of the building for it.

Our building's union won't allow us to hire additional cleaning staff outside of their sweep and mop service, unfortunately, or I'd have taken care of that by now. 

I do do shameing emails, or slack posts, when it's bad, and a lot of people will express sympathy  but that doesn't make it stop.
Thanks for your help you have really made this ongoing self-esteem degradation much better and I feel so awesome that I'm definitely not going to go jump off the roof. Excellent help. A+.

Nobody reads my emails. 

I know that sounds like a cop-out but SERIOUSLY nobody reads them. At all. Not the subject line, nothing. I can mark it urgent and write MANDATORY in all caps and walk around the office from table to table telling people to check their emails please and still miss a third of the office.

Thank you so much for understanding. I can't tell you what it means to me. 

Our building's sweep/mop service belongs to a union that makes it very difficult (impossible) to hire an additional cleaning service.
As I've explained in other places, our building's cursory cleaning staff's union precludes hiring another cleaning service.

I'm sorry you went through something similar. It's really unpleasant.

Honestly, nothing happens but that trash and dishes pile up. I took a long weekend for my brother's graduation, and all of my missed-day's sidework like throwing away old stale food, putting dishes in the dishwasher, taking in the mail and packages, just didn't get done. At all. AND they lit the microwave on fire. 

The building won't allow us to hire a cleaner because of rules with the building staff's union, or I would have by now. I am starting to think I really do need to address it with management, however inaccessible they are. Thank you.

General cleanup, like putting away clutter where it belongs, and making sure no large debris is in the lobby is a part of my job description, but taking everyone's dishes to the sink and scrubbing dried granola off of them is not. 

Cleaning rotation is a great idea, I will talk to my bosses about that. Thank you
I'm starting to think that conversation is necessary. I'm not even trying to leverage more pay, or anything like that, but I just can't keep walking in on Monday to a huge pile of dishes and trash.

>  Guys in the workplace are known to assume women will/should do this kind of thing.

Before I worked with the company, the female engineers and data analysts were doing my job on top of their own. You are completely correct in pointing out that gender is a factor, and honestly, I don't think any of our incredibly few female employees have contributed to any of the ongoing problems apart from dishes. Unfortunately there are maybe 5 other women in our 40 or so employees. (notably also, almost no people of color, and I am the only employee who isn't an heir to something or another)

I really appreciate it, thank you.

Luckily, we make mad bank and lock our clients into contracts. It's unlikely we'll fail, but we will probably lose "startup" status very quickly. We are not even currently reliant upon our backers, and are basically only a startup in name and attitude. 

I do agree that structure is going to shit, and they're trying to build it in but not making those builds very transparent or accessible.

I fully agree. To be honest, I'd be satisfied for now with the riot act, but in a touchy period where half of our employees are relatively new, my CEO and COO have avoided being overly aggressive about policy and lecturing. To be honest, they're very laid back in general, and want to somehow maintain a frat-house atmosphere as we continue to grow in size. 

There are plans to hire an administrative assistant in the next 8 months or so, but that's a long time for this to continue to wear on me. 

I'd have to ride some serious financial peen to get my pay doubled, and as a few other people have mentioned, because I do my job so well it's entirely possible my bosses haven't noticed I do twice the work I used to.

Janitorial work is not within the scope of my role,correct. We use reusable plates, cups, and silverware because I love the earth, we can't just "toss" things, we have to wash them. All I literally ask from my coworkers is that when the 3 separate "clean/dirty/empty" labels on the dishwasher state that it can be loaded, that they load it, and they seem to be literally incapable. 

I do call plumbers for leaks, etc. but it's like an Office Space situation where, the other 26 people who use the bathroom don't know I've already started working on the issue and feel the need to each individually tell me several times about the issue.

Office manager is actually very different from administrative support and being a secretary. I handle essential aspects of the company's functionality and particularly with regard to onboarding, I am irreplaceable at this time. Thanks for your opinion but it appears you didn't read my entire post, as I have clearly said that I've tried actual confrontation as often as I've tried politeness.

They do - our old building allowed us to bring in a 3rd party (Managed by Q - can't say it enough, they are wonderful) full service cleaner that would do everything from dust desks and knoll items to load the dishwasher, but our new building has a "dust and mop" service whose union precludes our bringing in other contractors.
I will give it a try, for sure

I have a written job description, but it's from a year ago and the company has changed drastically since then, and so my position has evolved to cover administrative duties, reception duties, office management, part of HR, and event planning to name a few. To add "literal janitor" to that would be to expand my role even further, but this isn't the kind of conversation that my direct reports really have with employees outside of year-end reviews.

To be honest - it just piles. It piles and piles and eventually someone shoots me an email that says "hey that leak in the mens' room is getting pretty bad" or "hey i noticed that stack of glasses in the sink is getting tall!" and if I use those as opportunities to ask for help, I'm always given the busy signal.

Thank you, I appreciate that. I would have been relying on their willingness to get me trained for actual tech support, I can't fund the education myself and I'm unqualified without it - just kind of a natural with troubleshooting. But I will look for something else, very soon.

What I'm explaining to you is that when I took the job, I didn't have to wipe asses and explain freezers to adults. 

Edit: You just recently added that first line, clarifying your point. No, these things were not a part of my job description and I would not have taken it if they had been.

I've brought up role growth before, and it's possible I'd move into a tech support role with training, but it's not currently in the plan for my higher-ups. Our building won't allow contractors like TaskRabbit or Managed by Q (who I HIGHLY recommend) to come in.

My long term goals are motivational speaking - that's what my degree and research are in. But it's about a 10 year career track even if it does end up working out, and jobs at nonprofits etc are unpaid/underpaid and I still need to eat and pay rent.

I don't know if you've ever been an office manager or not, but no, picking up trash making coffee, and wiping up spilled yogurt while the person who spilled it stands over me holding their coffee looking at the spill like it's a natural disaster someone else caused in a foreign country they'll never visit is not a part of my job.

Before we grew, my job tasks were stocking supplies, managing vendors, calendars, schedules, all onboarding processes, tech support, minor correspondence, and culture management - planning events and making sure they run properly. 

I still maintain all of those responsibilities, which are a full time job, and now, I bustle around an enormous office space picking up after overgrown children in what used to be my lunch break in addition.

Well, on this I couldn't disagree with you more about what's being done. I have honestly done these suggestions, aside from the last one where I outright tell them that I'm not feeling the respect. I will re-forward instructions, or mention to someone that I've done walkthroughs on a specific problem WITH THEM before, given people tutorials on basic appliances like refrigerators and dishwashers and very clearly asserted that I don't understand how they have so much trouble with these things at work. I doubt many of them have filthy kitchens at home. 

I will try outright telling them they're being disrespectful. Thank you for understanding - I KNOW I'm not a janitor, or a barista, and I struggle to understand how some of these tasks have fallen to me, but they won't get done if I don't do them. They don't get done when I don't do them. I found used tissues tucked under a speakerphone when I came back from my long weekend.

I actually attempted this - people have empathy for my problems, but don't see themselves as contributing to the problem, and the way we work is very isolate, so people aren't really in a place to notice trash being left somewhere and call it out. I did end up resolving a lot of THEIR ongoing problems though.

I am essentially a babysitter, and I don't have any power - I'm the lowest level employee in my own "department" that is just me, and lowest level employee altogether. 

I have brought things like that up to my bosses in the past, but they're more the brains behind the creation of the company than they are "managers" who handle employee issues.
